flags.description: Exports to the United States rose from 35% to 55% of gold exports between 2004 and 2005 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States fell from 56% to 24% of gold exports between 2008 and 2009 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to China rose from 41% to 67% of iron ore exports between 2008 and 2009 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to China fell from 32% to 12% of molybdenum exports between 2009 and 2010 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States rose from 2% to 25% of silver exports between 2015 and 2016 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States rose from 5% to 28% of gold exports between 2016 and 2017 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Documented commitments from China's institutions reached US$3.0 bn in 2018, 1% of GDP; the largest: China CITIC Bank Corporation Limited (US$1.3 bn).

flags.description: Exports to China rose from 64% to 86% of iron ore exports between 2018 and 2019 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to China rose from 3% to 29% of molybdenum exports between 2019 and 2020 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to China rose from 41% to 68% of lithium exports between 2021 and 2022 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).
Exports to the United States rose from 6% to 26% of gold exports between 2022 and 2023 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).

sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 42.0 for China (band 33.3–56.6, from 3 of six components) and 12.0 for the United States (band 9.3–50.4, from 4 of six components). The net lean is +30.0 points toward China.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China rose by 2.6 points and the index for the United States rose by 7.0 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 48% of Chile's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$68.4 bn) went to China and 14% to the United States; together 61%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China fell by 6.4 points and the share going to the United States rose by 6.4 points.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in molybdenum (RCA 2.2), copper (RCA 1.8) and lithium (RCA 1.6).

10 sudden shifts in export shares are flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2023: Exports to the United States rose from 6% to 26% of gold exports between 2022 and 2023 (reported by CHL to UN Comtrade).

Since 2019, agreement with China fell by 10.1 points and agreement with the United States rose by 18.6 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After Section 301 tariffs on imports from China, first tranche in force (2018-07), the share of exports to China moved +7.8 points (42% before, 50% after); placebo p 0.25 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After Peru: Chancay port (COSCO Shipping Ports majority) inaugurated (2024-11), the share of exports to China moved -6.6 points (54% before, 48% after); placebo p 0.41 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States prohibited (Announcement 2024 No. 46) (2024-12), the share of exports to China moved -6.6 points (54% before, 48% after); placebo p 0.41 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

Relative to the countries outside its scope, Chile: Estrategia Nacional del Litio announced (state participation through Codelco/ENAMI, CEOL contracts) is followed by a +2.6 points difference-in-differences in the share of exports to the United States (permutation p 0.40).

Relative to the countries outside its scope, Chile: Estrategia Nacional del Litio announced (state participation through Codelco/ENAMI, CEOL contracts) is followed by a -5.4 points difference-in-differences in the share of exports to China (permutation p 0.39).

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to China in 2030 is 56% (90% band 40%–75%), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 13% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 14% (90% band 3.7%–22%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 44.1 (90% band 33.3–57.5), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 11.7 (90% band 0.7–23.5), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 2% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.
Under the stated scenarios the 2030 median share to China ranges from 46% (US sourcing rules bite) to 66% (accelerated China pull); these are what-ifs with a fixed yearly shift, not predictions.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
15 of the dated events used above are still in the draft event list awaiting the project owner's review.
Stance values come from the text model (zero-shot baseline, not yet validated); the rest of this brief rests on official statistics and the registered databases, each cited on its chart.

human.title: Chile: the copper that ties the region to China, and the one place the United States still buys
human.author: AI-drafted from the site's indicators; not yet reviewed by the project owner
human.text_md:
## Alignment

Chile's index leans toward China, 42.0 against 11.9 in 2024 [index_value:influence:CN:2024] [index_value:influence:US:2024], and its trade is the largest in the region: US$68.4 bn of mineral exports in 2025, 48% to China and 14% to the United States, the highest US share of any country with a China lean [concentration:share_cn_x:2025] [concentration:share_us_x:2025]. Copper is US$58.6 bn of it, US$29.8 bn to China and US$8.7 bn to the United States [flow_trade:CHL:copper:2025]. The executives' coded statements are measured toward both powers (+0.20 toward the United States over ten, 0.00 toward China over three) [statement:stance_us:CHL:2024-2026] [statement:stance_cn:CHL:2024-2026]. Lithium takes 51% of the mineral mentions and 3.2% of the export value; copper is 86% of the value and a third of the mentions [insights:talk_vs_trade_minerals:CHL]. My reading: Chile is the country where the United States could matter commercially, because it already buys a seventh of the copper, and the one where the political conversation is least about that.

## Trajectory

The Chinese share of exports rose from 19% in 2008 to 44% in 2016 and 54% in 2020, then eased to 48% in 2025 [concentration:share_cn_x:2020] [concentration:share_cn_x:2025]. Ten sudden trade shifts are flagged, the most in the region [anomaly_flag:sudden_trade_shift]. Chinese commitments were US$4.9 bn over 2015–2021, US$3.0 bn of it in 2018, the year of the Tianqi stake in SQM; the US record is small, US$24 m of DFC and EXIM commitments in 2015–2021 and US$8 m in 2022–2024 [flow_finance:CN:CHL:2018] [flow_finance:US:CHL:2015-2021] [flow_finance:US:CHL:2022-2024]. The window after China's 2024 antimony controls shows the share to the United States rising 4.9 points (placebo p 0.04), one of the few policy windows in the region with a US-side movement in that direction; the 2023 national lithium strategy shows no difference against the other countries (−3.2 points toward the United States, permutation p 1.00) [event_effect:cn_export_control_antimony:US:window:CHL] [event_effect:chl_national_lithium_strategy:US:did:CHL]. The legislature's coded records are too few to score (two in 2024) [document:stance_us:CHL:2024]; the index's five-year change is +7.0 for the United States and +2.7 for China [index_value:influence:US:2024] [index_value:influence:CN:2024].

## Risks and likely next moves

The models put China's share at 56% in 2030 at baseline, 66% under the China pull and 46% under US reshoring; the US share reaches 24% under reshoring, the highest among the countries whose exports go mostly to China [forecast:export_share:CN:baseline:2030:CHL] [forecast:export_share:US:us_reshoring:2030:CHL]. Parity would take US$11.6 bn of yearly copper switching, 1.2 times what the United States already buys, and copper alone could cover it [insights:parity_gap:CHL]. The Section 232 copper proclamation of 2025 exempts ores, concentrates and cathodes, so in my reading it changes little for Chile directly [event:us_section232_copper]; the Codelco–SQM lithium company and the new lithium contracts decide where the second mineral goes. The risk is price: a copper price swing revalues the Chinese and American bills in the same proportion and moves no share at all [price:copper].

## What would change this reading

A 2026 trade year in which the US copper share moved by more than the scenario's two points; a US commitment in the finance record above the few million dollars a year recorded so far; a lithium contract with a non-Chinese offtaker large enough to show in the lithium rows; or a reviewed event list.
